title: Somalia South-Central drought — 2020-2023
brief_outcome_free: South-central Somalia (Bay region). Agropastoral livelihoods, chronic food insecurity, and a history of consecutive failed rains driving severe drought. You are the DOC drought analyst.

act1_quiz.prompt: It is September 2020 and you are assessing the seasonal outlook for south-central Somalia. Which large-scale climate pattern active at this time would you flag as raising the risk of poor Deyr (October-December) rains?
act1_quiz.hint: Both the Pacific and the Indian Ocean modulate the Horn of Africa short rains.
options: Developing La Nina conditions in the Pacific combined with a negative Indian Ocean Dipole
A strong El Nino warming the eastern Pacific
A positive Indian Ocean Dipole enhancing onshore moisture flow
The Madden-Julian Oscillation locked in a wet phase over East Africa
act1_quiz.correct: Developing La Nina conditions in the Pacific combined with a negative Indian Ocean Dipole
act1_quiz.answer_note: In late 2020 La Nina was establishing in the Pacific while the Indian Ocean Dipole was negative. Both patterns are associated with suppressed October-December (Deyr) short rains over the eastern Horn of Africa, so the seasonal forecast deficit has a physically plausible driver behind it.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Context that conditions how strongly the SEAS5 forecast-deficit evidence should be weighted at long lead.

act1_quiz.prompt: Bay region's agropastoral system depends on two rainy seasons each year - the Gu (April-June) and the Deyr (October-December). Why does a forecast of another below-normal season carry extra weight here?
act1_quiz.hint: Think about what happens when households cannot recover between seasons.
options: Consecutive failed seasons compound: depleted water, pasture and seed stocks leave no buffer before the next season
A single bad season is always enough to cause famine regardless of history
The two seasons are independent, so a failure in one says nothing about overall risk
Irrigated farming dominates here, so rainfall seasons matter little
act1_quiz.correct: Consecutive failed seasons compound: depleted water, pasture and seed stocks leave no buffer before the next season
act1_quiz.answer_note: Drought here is slow-onset and multi-season. Each poor Gu or Deyr drains household reserves - water, pasture, livestock condition, seeds - so the marginal effect of the next poor season grows. A deficit forecast on top of an already-dry SPI-3 signals compounding risk, not an isolated event.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Explains why the current SPI-3 state and the forecast deficit jointly raise risk more than either alone.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: Forecast deficit and CDI agree months ahead of the event window. This is a STRONG, early signal. What DOC level do you set, and what anticipatory action does the ~6-month lead justify?

counterfactual.prompt: What if anticipatory action (anticipatory cash, water trucking and supplementary feeding) were triggered at the lead round on the strong forecast signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Slow-onset droughts give long lead. The counterfactual shows the loss-reduction value of acting on a confident seasonal signal rather than waiting for impact confirmation.
